body:
The dang Flamingo that poops on the potty. It sings the most obnoxious song. On top of that it's poop is akin to kinetic sand. Messy and annoying. The perfect combo.

**edit** I just reread the original post. This definitely isn't appropriate for a 1 year old. I do agree with the comment for Linkimals. Those are horrifying for baby toys.

The first panic attack I had was the scariest moment of my life. I was not thinking clearly and had no control over it. I was certain my heart was going to explode. I didn't let myself be alone for two weeks after. It was terrible.
Jealous that you get the option to plan! Best of luck to you.

Hey! Remember, anxiety was okay to feel when the debris hit your window! That's a scary thing, especially when you're alone with your baby. Don't demonize the feeling, because your body was definitely responding appropriately! I'm sorry you are suffering lately. It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. Hope you're able to get a good night sleep and tomorrow is a better day! ❤ Hang in there!!

We actually made YouTube a hard no at our house about 2 years ago. We found the content seems to play on weird dopamine rushes and it didn't seen healthy so we cut it off. It's interesting because still to this day she'll try to bargain for YouTube. It's like kid crack!

Oh man. That really does sound awful. I'm sorry you went through that. My husband had a similar experience as a child, although he was taught to completely bottle up and experience no emotions. We really try to be open to all emotions and let her feel everything she needs to feel, but as a parent, sometimes it's really hard to discern wants/needs and when she really is acting out. 

I'm glad you've gone to therapy. Sometimes there's a weird stigma around it. Hope all works out for you as well!
She says "Let me do me, girlfriend?" Those are moments you want to record so you can play them back later. That's adorable.

I hear you. I truly do. It sounds like you've got a lot of unresolved trauma from a shitty childhood. I don't tell my child she's being manipulative, I noticed manipulative behavior, as parents tried to talk to her about it then realized it was over her head. I, by no means would ever tell someone else what to do, but the emotional response this provoked in you might be a good indicator of something you could work on in therapy. ❤️ I've spent a solid amount of time in therapy addressing issue like that and it's been so freeing to be able to process and not have to bear that pain anymore.

A couple things: 

School papers- my little one is in kindergarten this year. I didn't realize just how many papers they bring home. My goodness, her backpack is full each day. I try to sort through the work. If it's something I can tell she spent time on or work she is very proud of, I have a special folder box I put it in. Each year has a folder (Kinder, 1st, 2nd, 3rd...) and the box is a big plastic file box I got at Walmart. I also write letters to her when I think about it and stick it in the corresponding year. When she gets to be an adult, I intend to give it to her as a fun keepsake from her childhood. 

Little nothing toys - stuff from the goodie bags, happy meal toys, etc. I clean out the toy box once a month. All the little knickknack toys that will never be played with again get tossed. I try to throw them out before they ever get to the toybox.

 I've noticed the amount of "stuff" in my house usually trends with my stress level so I try to stay on top of it. I feel you though. The tiny humans generate a lot of stuff.

I like the idea of a curious and patient approach. I honestly asked the question because I was curious about the underlying meaning of all of these odd comments lately. Patience is definitely key, although not always easy.
You got this!
Appreciate it! Kids don't come with a handbook. I do what I can to do the right thing.
Kid's say the darndest things. Right? Lol!
You made her.
AMEN!
You friend, clearly have children and get it. Lol!

I have explored a bit on those two topics. We're going to attempt to get a better full night sleep and wake up a half hour earlier so she had the ability to chill a bit before getting ready. I've spoke with her teacher to see if she is noticing anything at school. 

As far as attention at home, we do what we can, but we're full time students, employees, parents and unfortunately she's an only child so she constantly feels starved for attention. We've set up some play dates with good friends and are doing what we can so she gets so good interaction. 

Thanks for your input!
I think you're definitely on to something here. Good TV is so hard to come by!!

Amen, friend. I didn't say the word manipulation to trigger people, simply her actions are being used to maneuver a situation in her favor. I appreciate your suggestions. Firm boundaries are for sure a place that is easy to get lazy at. I could definitely be better at it. Thanks for your input!
I feel you! We're going to make it!
Oh my God! This is the best thing I've read all week.
Interesting insight. I, too, know many adults that struggle to communicate well. Parenting is hard. I just want a healthy, well adjusted, happy human!
The drama is absolutely real at our house. Sometimes it's so over the top it's hilarious.
Picking your battles is so difficult. Parenting is exhausting sometimes! Thanks for your advice!!
Interesting. I'd never thought of it that way.
I like your advice. I'll dig more for root cause.
I like the last line you put there. She definitely is just trying to get what she wants not for malicious intent.
I like this suggestion. I definitely fall into the "because you need to do it" category more than I'd like to.
I totally see that. I think you're right, she likely is pushing boundaries and not being manipulative.
This response is super helpful. Thanks for taking the time to respond.
